title: Article 45 — Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years

content.overview: Article 45 (as substituted by the 86th Amendment) directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. (Free and compulsory education for children from six to fourteen is now a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.)
content.glance: State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for children until age six. (6–14 education is Art 21A FR.)
content.study:
The 86th Amendment restructured the education scheme: Article 21A (Fundamental Right to free and compulsory education for 6–14); Article 45 redirected to early childhood care and education below six; Article 51A(k) added a parental/guardian duty.

Examination: below six; early childhood care and education; contrast Art 21A for 6–14; 86th Amendment.

sections.heading: Key directive
sections.body: Endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 45 provide after the 86th Amendment?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: After the 86th Amendment, Article 45 directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. Free and compulsory education for children from six to fourteen years is a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.

keyTakeaways: Art 45: early childhood care and education below age six.
